subject.title: RFC 0009: align Hosted Feed v1 specifications

question: Should RFC 0009 accept the full reusable snapshot, query, delta, and trust contract now, or limit v1 to the publisher-feed subset already closest to implementation?
rationale: The branch turns draft design text into a broad normative compatibility and trust contract; source review cannot choose the permanent v1 scope or authorize its security model without maintainer intent.

options.title: Require synchronized full-v1 proof
options.body: Keep the full contract, but merge only after the linked OpenClaw and ClawHub branches demonstrate interoperable positive and negative cases against this exact RFC head.

options.title: Narrow v1 to publisher feeds
options.body: Limit the accepted contract to publisher snapshots and the minimal trust path, leaving generalized catalog sharding, queries, and deltas as later addenda.

options.title: Accept as design baseline
options.body: Merge the broad draft as an explicitly provisional design baseline and accept that implementations may still force compatibility-sensitive revisions.

recommendation.title: Require synchronized full-v1 proof
recommendation.body: Keep the full contract, but merge only after the linked OpenClaw and ClawHub branches demonstrate interoperable positive and negative cases against this exact RFC head.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick reviewed and materially shaped the original hosted-feed model and is the strongest available independent routing candidate for the scope decision.
